Q1: 2-Phenoxyethanol exhibits known hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, or reproductive hazards, as well as oral and dermal/eye exposure, based on official GHS classifications. Inhalation hazards have an expanded perspective of concern (Tier 2). While environmental hazards are considered low to moderate (Tier 3), data for endocrine disruption and organ/systemic hazards are currently deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: While not on explicit lists of concern, 2-Phenoxyethanol is included on the SCIL Yellow Triangle list, signifying it meets Safer Choice criteria as a best-in-class functional ingredient despite some remaining hazard profile issues. Additionally, it is listed in the FDA's "Substances Added to Food" inventory, indicating its regulation and use as a food or color additive.
Q3: This chemical is extensively characterized, with 19,000 literature references, significantly exceeding the median for the specialized dataset of fracking and petrochemical materials. Its precise molecular formula (C8H10O2) and classification as a "Small Molecule," rather than an ill-defined substance or UVCB, further confirm its well-defined nature, although there are still data gaps in its endocrine disruption and organ/systemic hazard profiles.
